MCD.rationale: McDonald's presents a high-quality, durable franchise with structurally high margins (operating ~45%, net ~31%) and robust cash generation ($2.41B quarterly OCF), supported by a 95%-franchised asset-light model. Q1 2026 results showed solid YoY growth (+9.4% revenue, +6.9% EPS) and beat consensus estimates, validating the business model's resilience. However, several factors temper conviction: (1) meaningful sequential deceleration (QoQ revenue -7.9%, EPS -12.6%, OCF -29.6%) with management itself flagging consumer spending 'getting a little bit worse' and expecting Q2 sales deceleration; (2) negative shareholders' equity of -$1.29B in a rising-rate environment (10Y at 4.47%, 2Y up 49bps) creates structural refinancing risk for a heavily leveraged balance sheet; (3) elevated oil ($96.83/bbl) pressures input costs; (4) reliable valuation data is unavailable (PE_diluted=0 across all observations), preventing confident assessment of cheapness vs. own history. The stock is near its 52-week low ($272.72 vs $271.85) and down -16.7% quarterly, which may reflect some de-risking, but without clean valuation metrics the entry point cannot be confirmed as genuinely attractive. The franchise quality and margin durability support a mildly positive view, but the balance-sheet leverage, macro headwinds, and sequential cooling cap conviction at the low end of the positive range.
